nodes.title: director21: 16 lessons (4 pilot topics x steady, stuck, offtopic, steering), Director only, reactive rule-based child, int/r6 1697dcc54 (integration 52), 1,733 model calls, about $1.27; four Opus judges at high effort, one per topic, hand counts. Result: c5-t01 passes the scale gate on every line (first time); c4, c5-t02 and c6 fail (c6 passed in director20). Words against the board 1 / 0 / 1 / 3 (c4, c5-t01, c5-t02, c6); unsaid boards 2 / 0 / 1 / 0; misgrades 0; false keys 0; verdicts 74/74, 67/67, 75/75, 71/71. Axes d20 to d21: listening 3 to 3, 3 to 3.5, 3 to 3, 3.5 to 3; register 3.5 to 3, 3 to 3.5, 3.5 to 3, 3.5 to 3; promises 3.5 to 4, 2.5 to 4, 3 to 3.5, 3.5 to 3.5; class level 4 in all four. 13 of 13 parks returned. Aside replies: 24, of which 3 odd (all re-renders), 15 flat, 6 natural. Second clarifies: 8, all merely repeat. Question-only re-asks short of their givens: 15 of 70. backTo used 0 times in 33 returns to an earlier card. The run's own predicate check read 0 on every gated predicate. Judgement: docs/design/round7/judgements/director21-2026-11-11.md; results: evals/hybrid-side-by-side/results/2026-11-11-director21/.

After director21: the order of a lesson is a law, and the ending and the seams are authored. Order laws O1 to O7, each a predicate failing on director21's rows first, gated dry and run over every live run: a unit's parts are said in order and none is skipped; a return, an AI line or a request reply never takes a part's place; a remediation only after its own misconception answer on its own board, never as help; a request stays on the part it was asked about; a turn with no unit says nothing about a figure and no other unit's board is up; the first miss never gets the key and a clarify spends no help; her answer to the child's question comes first in its turn. E1: each script gets an authored teachback (question, key, board) and wrap; the model writes none of the ending. C1: second wordings for every point, why and worked problem; no authored sentence of 6 or more words in two consecutive turns. J1 (clause 2, register below director20 in three topics): backTo fires, four new authored seam joints, a predicate that no two parts meet without a joint; the model joins only if register stays below 3.5 in two or more topics in the next run. S2: Learning marks ask on cards whose last sentence cannot stand alone; the whole card after the second miss. R2/R3: the aside reply is said once; forms take the child's phrase of up to three words. The walk reads the compiled cells for every column (compile step 3). The staged 30 stay held. Reverse if: a displaced part said late makes lessons rigid (more than 2 rows a topic, two judges); the authored wrap reads as a form letter to two judges; more than half of second wordings judged unhelpful; register still below 3.5 in two topics (then the model joins); a restated phrase misstates the child in more than 1 reply in 10.

director21's live rows read 0 on every gated dry predicate (27 predicates) and the four judges then counted 5 contradictions and 3 unsaid boards by hand. Every predicate had been written from director20's rows; director21's faults were new orderings (a return displacing a part, a remediation used as help, a picture request leaving its part, an unscripted ending with a stale board), and no predicate looked at turns without a unit or at the order of a unit's parts. A predicate set built from the last run's faults does not bound the next run's. The hand count stays the gate until the order of a lesson is itself checked.

No judged run before director21 reached the end of a script. With the steady lesson run to the end, the teach-back and wrap were heard for the first time: model-written, with no unit and no board of their own, they produced 3 of the run's 5 contradictions (c6 steady 114 to 120), affirmed non-answers in three topics and praised work the child never did. A part of the lesson that no run exercises is unjudged, whatever the gate reads.

Tried (L1 and L2 of dc-r8-director20, Brain c7f18ae5): after a key, a give-up or a clarify gets the key and its why again, at most twice. What broke in director21: the same why was said three turns running with only its opener rotated (c4 stuck 12 to 16 and 36 to 40, c5-t01 stuck 34 to 38, c5-t02 stuck 28 to 32, c6 stuck 24 to 28 and steering 16 to 20); all 8 second clarifies merely repeated; judges scored it as not listening. Replaced by authored second wordings and a rule that no authored sentence is said in two consecutive turns.
